ideas.thesis: The sleeve is 100% US (VTI 52%, VOO 30%, cash 18%) while the US index is a record 42% "AI Big Ten". VXUS is below its 50d (-2.83%) at RSI 40, cheaper than US. A Bogle global-cap mix argues for adding it with the scheduled DCA.

ideas.whyRejected: Already 52% of NAV; adding more US total-market deepens the same megacap concentration. Next DCA turn.
0.7% off its 52w high and overlaps VTI; no reason to prefer it over diversifying today.
Bogle persona does not sell to time rates or AI headlines; selling would only realize cost and SEC fees.

decision.summary: Do one DCA ticket of about $10 into VXUS at midday to start the international sleeve, keep about $13 cash, and sell nothing.
decision.reasoning: Value is a buy-and-hold DCA sleeve, not a timing sleeve. The research did not change the rule (keep buying broad index funds) but did change where the next dollar goes. US cap-weighted indexes are now unusually concentrated (record 42% in ten AI names; equal weight lagging by the widest margin in 24 years), and the sleeve has zero ex-US. VXUS is the only fund in the allowlist below its 50-day. Rates at 5.2% and a likely December hike are a reason to keep a cash buffer, not a reason to sell index funds. I will buy at midday after the open settles, since Value only does one order a day.

plan.trigger: Always (scheduled DCA), unless the sleeve cash would drop below $10

risks: A stronger dollar on higher US rates can weigh on VXUS in USD terms.
Small tickets: fractional ETF fills are modeled; real brokers may not allow fractional ETF shares (Schwab Stock Slices covers S&P 500 stocks only).
CPI on Oct 14 could move everything; DCA accepts that.
